facts.question: Is there more or less snow than on the same date last winter, and why?
notes: model values = SnowScope snow history at one height of each resort (an estimate for an area)
measured values = a snow station on the date given (one point), only where a station history exists
days with a gain of 10 cm or more = snowfall days this winter; days with a loss of 5 cm or more = melt, rain or wind

en.title: More snow than last winter in the US Northeast? 0 of 4 resorts ahead (12 November)
en.description: On 12 November, four US Northeast resorts have less snow than a year ago. Gore Mountain is down 6 cm (2 in). SnowScope snow history, 12 Nov 2026.
en.lede: Early season snow in the Northeast has not caught up with last winter yet. On 12 November, none of the four resorts we checked are ahead of their depth from the same date in 2025-26. The gap is small at Killington Resort but sharper at Gore Mountain, which sits 6 cm (2 in) below where it stood a year ago.

p: Killington Resort holds 5 cm (2 in) today, matching its 5 cm (2 in) on 12 November last winter. At this time of year, the usual depth is only 1 cm (0 in), so Killington is running ahead of the November average despite being level with last year.

Gore Mountain shows the steepest slide: 1 cm (0 in) today versus 7 cm (3 in) a year ago. This is the biggest gap among the four sites. For this date, the normal snow depth is 0 cm (0 in), so even thin snow is ahead of a typical early season.

Stratton sits at 1 cm (0 in), down from 4 cm (2 in) on the same date in 2025-26. Okemo Mountain has 0 cm (0 in) today compared with 4 cm (2 in) last year. Both mountains are thin, though again this is not unusual for mid-November.

None of the four resorts have recorded a single day with 10 cm (4 in) or more of new snow so far this winter. This explains why they are behind or at best level with last year at this point. Early November was quiet across the region.

There have also been no major melt or wind-loss days at any of these mountains, so the small amounts that fell have stayed put. The difference is simply that November storms have not yet arrived with real snow.

Last winter (2025-26) was generous in January. Killington Resort peaked at 64 cm (25 in) on 26 January. Gore Mountain reached 84 cm (33 in) on the same date. Stratton topped out at 67 cm (26 in) in late January. Okemo Mountain built to 58 cm (23 in) at its peak.
These peaks came months after mid-November, so the early season snow depth tells little about how much snow fell later. Last winter's main storms arrived in the new year, not the fall.

Across the US Northeast on 12 November, SnowScope shows snow on 2,930 km² and at 17 of 111 resorts. Only 190 km² and 4 resorts had snow two days earlier. The region is building up fast, though still early in the season.

By 15 November, the forecast shows snow could cover 19,660 km² and reach 39 resorts. A significant storm is expected in the next few days. When that hits, the year-on-year comparison will likely shift.

sections.h: Why mid-November numbers matter less than you think
p: Whether a resort is 2 cm (1 in) ahead or behind on a single day in November is not predictive. The ski season's character is set by what falls from December onward. One or two dry weeks in December can erase any early advantage, and a good January can build a base from almost nothing.
The mountains on this list have all seen their real snow seasons arrive much later—typically in January or February. November is a teaser, not a promise.

advice: Watch the next few days of forecasts: the region is due for significant snow that will reshape this comparison quickly.
These numbers are SnowScope estimates at one height on each mountain; ground truth varies by slope, elevation and aspect. Use the map to see where snow is concentrated.
Early December and January will tell you far more about how this winter will play out than November depth alone.
Before heading off-piste or into the backcountry, check the official avalanche bulletin for your area, even if the base is thin.
Confirm that a resort is open and which lifts are running on its website before you drive; snow on the map does not mean the mountain is operating.
